# Process

## Idea

### Content assembly line
<a id="proc-assembly-line"></a>

Ideation → creation → editing per platform → distribution (post and engage) → analyse. Batching (a 12-hour day of 3–4 videos) works for some but often adds pressure that hurts performance.

`idea` · formats: reel30, reel60, reel90, yt-short, yt-long, carousel, story, podcast · niches: all · stated · from [L05](../sources/L05.md)

Related: [Theme first, then plan, shots, edit, copy](../topics/process.md#proc-theme-first-workflow), [Edit blueprint per video](../topics/process.md#proc-edit-blueprint)

### Six pillars of content
<a id="proc-six-pillars"></a>

Strategy (state the goal in one sentence), ideation, scripting, talent/energy management (teleprompter, mornings, let a yapper talk 4–8 min), editing, growth tactics.

> there's six pillars to content.

`idea` · formats: reel30, reel60, reel90, yt-short, yt-long, carousel, story, podcast · niches: all · stated · from [L08](../sources/L08.md)

Related: [Community content: involve, converse, showcase](../topics/ideas.md#ideas-audience-as-hero)

### Theme first, then plan, shots, edit, copy
<a id="proc-theme-first-workflow"></a>

Our order: research and 3 theme options → content plan → shot list/footage audit → edit blueprint → copy pack → publishing plan → review after 24–72 h.

## Script

### Seed + reference layout → many rewrites
<a id="proc-seed-reference-rewrites"></a>

Harry's ad: a seed line, a conflict list, a borrowed reference layout, 2 days and 25 rewrites, spitballing without judging (let the dirty tap water run clean), feedback from people with taste, then a design pass.

> The only way… you can make this ad is if you build it up piece by piece by piece.

`script` · formats: reel30, reel60, reel90, yt-short, yt-long, carousel, story, podcast · niches: all · stated · from [L09](../sources/L09.md)

### Write 4–5 versions side by side
<a id="proc-four-five-versions"></a>

Write several versions for freedom to be wrong; showing three versions gets far better feedback than one ("use that sentence, but put it in that one").

`script` · formats: reel30, reel60, reel90, yt-short, yt-long, carousel, story, podcast · niches: all · stated · from [L09](../sources/L09.md)

### Draft in the final tool, judge in context
<a id="proc-write-in-final-tool"></a>

Write the newsletter in ConvertKit and ads in Figma as readers will see them; test a billboard among seven other ads with people walking by.

> I never do anything which is not on the tool I'm using, ever.

### Who, what to say, how to say it
<a id="proc-who-say-how"></a>

Copywriting's three pieces: who you're talking to (and what they're doing then), having something to say, saying it well; move them from current to desired attitude.

> Who am I talking to? You got to have something to say and you got to say it well. That's copywriting.

### Storyboard table before any edit
<a id="l10-storyboard-before-edit"></a>

Before Claude touches the footage (he does it even before shooting), it writes the whole video as a table: every line, what is on screen, which tool makes it. You fix the plan and agree on it, then Claude builds the edit from it. Chandler's columns: # / Freeze (time) / Chandler says / On screen.

**How:** Prompt: "Before editing anything, write the storyboard as a table: # | time | what I say | on screen | tool | sound cue. Wait for my OK." Review it, change rows, then say "build it".

> Before Claude edits anything, have it write a storyboard, so that you both agree on what the video looks like first. I always do this before I shoot.

`script` · formats: reel30, reel60, reel90, yt-short, yt-long · niches: all · stated · from [L10](../sources/L10.md) · ⚠ [C30](../clashes.md#c30)

## Edit

### Edit blueprint per video
<a id="proc-edit-blueprint"></a>

Our template: theme, format and length, audio, 0–2 s hook, timestamped timeline, cut rules, text, grade, sound design, cover frame, export, app steps.

## Graphics

### Copy and design are one
<a id="proc-copy-design-one"></a>

Harry can't separate copy and design: fit key lines on one line, bold the rhythm words ("twice", "both") in a design pass, and make illustrations match the story (the money-thrower looks annoyed).

> Copy… and design are one of the same. Like I can't do them differently.

## Publish

### Only 9/10+ ships; walk around the garden
<a id="proc-nine-ten-standard"></a>

Your work is your standards: nine out of ten or it doesn't go out; it's done when nothing can be added or taken away.

> your work is nothing but your standards. Nine out of 10 plus, it goes out. If not, you won't see it.

<a id="proc-brick-by-brick"></a>

> it's not a boulder that builds a building. It's brick by brick.

## Mindset

### Be excited; light people up
<a id="mind-light-people-up"></a>

Be excited and have fun or it won't do well. People want to hear from someone at their level or one above; nobody is too old or too niche.

> You are there to light people up

### Confidence comes from evidence
<a id="mind-confidence-from-evidence"></a>

Confidence comes from evidence, evidence from effort. Niches make saturation not real: maybe three in a thousand actually put in the work.

`mindset` · formats: reel30, reel60, reel90, yt-short, yt-long, carousel, story, podcast · niches: all · stated · from [L08](../sources/L08.md)

### Results over ego
<a id="mind-results-over-ego"></a>

Don't let insecurity stop you posting; look at the metrics. Iteration over perfection: comfort doesn't build iconic brands. If friends on Instagram make you nervous, start on TikTok.

> comfort doesn't build iconic brands
